newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT -JGBs seen edging down, eyes on stocks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -JGBs seen edging down, eyes on stocks.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to trade with a downward bias on Friday on carry-over weakness from Thursday's late trade.
June's try at the upside failed on Thursday, confirming that JGBs were top-heavy, traders said.
"June JGBs are likely to feel heavy above 124.00 today as well. There are resistance points at 124.19 and 124.23," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
There will be some focus on April money supply data due at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT), traders said.
If growth in M2+CDs comes in at three percent or above, there is likely to be a negative impact on JGBs, said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
Economists' polled by Reuters gave forecasts for growth in the April M2+CDs money supply average ranging from 2.5 percent to 2.8 percent.
The downside for JGBs is likely to be limited, however, if the yen rises against the dollar during Friday's Tokyo trade and pushes down Tokyo share prices, the first trader said.
The dollar closed in New York overnight at 115.75/85 yen and was quoted at 116.20/25 yen as of 2328 GMT.

Reported comments by a senior Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) official that Japan may face pressure to raise interest rates led to some selling of JGBs in London overnight, but the impact was limited, the first trader said.

Jiji news agency quoted Koichi Kato, secretary-general of the ruling LDP, as saying late on Thursday that Japan may face pressure to change its current low interest rate levels as it progresses with financial market deregulation.
